title: Target Sum
prompt:
Put a `+` or `-` in front of each number in `nums` and add them up. Return the number of different sign assignments whose total equals `target`.

**Example**: `nums = [1,1,1,1,1]`, `target = 3` → `5` (one `-` in any of the five positions).

**Constraints**: `1 <= nums.length <= 20`, `0 <= nums[i] <= 1000`, `sum(nums) <= 1000`, `-1000 <= target <= 1000`.
hints: Brute force tries 2ⁿ sign choices. As you work through the numbers left to right, what's the only thing about your earlier choices that still matters?
Let the state be (index i, running sum), and ways(i, sum) = ways(i+1, sum + nums[i]) + ways(i+1, sum - nums[i]). Running sums can be negative, so memoize in a HashMap (or shift indexes by total).

Algebra shortcut: if P is the sum of the `+` numbers, then P - (total - P) = target, so P = (total + target) / 2. Count subsets summing to P with `dp[j] += dp[j - x]` going downwards. Return 0 if the parity is wrong or |target| > total.

solution.explanation: Every assignment splits the numbers into a plus set P and a minus set, with P - (total - P) = target. So the number of assignments equals the number of subsets summing to (total + target) / 2. Counting those is a 0/1 knapsack with j going downwards. Zeros are counted correctly because each can be in the subset or not. O(n · P) time, O(P) space; the memo on (i, sum) is O(n · total).
